mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying, the Exalted: (إن كل نفس لما عليها): whoever reads (لما) without doubling makes (ما) redundant (zāʾida) and (إن) lightened from the heavy one; what follows it is nominative because of its deficiency [i.e. having lost its governing force]. It is the answer to the oath, as if He said "every soul — over it is surely a guardian"; its proper form is "over every soul there is surely a guardian". So (حافظ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (لعليها) is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of (كل). The lām entered and is obligatory to distinguish between the (إن) lightened from the heavy one and the (إن) meaning negating (ما). Whoever doubles (لما) makes (لما) mean (إلا) and (إن) mean (ما), its implied form being "There is no soul but that over it is a guardian". Sībawayh reported (نشدتك الله لما فعلت), i.e. "I adjure you by Allah, only do (إلا فعلت)".

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (يوم تبلى السرائر): (يوم) is an adverbial, and its governor is (لقادر). (رجعه) does not govern it, because you would then be separating the ṣila (relative clause) from its relative [i.e. the maṣdar from what it governs] by the khabar (predicate) of (إن). This is according to the view of whoever says that (رجعه) means His resurrecting him and reviving him after his death. As for whoever says (رجعه) means returning the water into the urethra, or says returning the old man to his states from the sperm-drop, or holding back the water so that it does not come out of the urethra, he makes (يوما) accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "remember the day when [secrets] are tested"; (لقادر) does not govern it [on this view], because He did not mean that He is able to return the water into the urethra and the rest on the Day of Resurrection; He only informed that He is able to do it in this world, were He to will it.
